text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: service=serving-runtime, symptom=OOM & container restarts, group=kv-paged-allocator, region=us-west-2. 23 failures in 12m. https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/8234

sre-alex: ack — I'm taking lead. tagging infra and runtime eng.

eng-carol: pulling logs from the affected pod pool now (runtime-kv-pool-3-*). Seeing repeated CUDA OOM followed by container restart loop. Sample from pod runtime-kv-3-7f9b: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.72 GiB total capacity; 28.10 GiB already allocated)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/allocator.py", line 412, in allocate_chunk
    ptr = cuda_malloc(size)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/cuda/memory.py", line 78, in cuda_malloc
    raise RuntimeError('CUDA OOM')
```

infra-miguel: node events show OOM kills + kubelet marking NotReady briefly on several nodes. dmesg on node-aws-usw2-17 shows: ``[12345.678] Out of memory: Kill process 38291 (runtime) score 1000 or sacrifice child``

eng-carol: also seeing the runtime's internal metrics: `kv_cache_total_bytes` rising steadily per pod over hours, and `paged_allocator_frag_ratio` creeping from 0.12 to 0.48 on affected hosts. Not reclaimed between requests.

support-lina: customer-facing impact: support/alerts show increased 500s and 503s for a small set of high-context requests. Two customers (acme-corp, radiant-ai) filed incidents; error rate at ~4.8% vs baseline 0.2%.

sre-alex: hypothesis: slow memory bleed in the paged-attention / KV cache allocator leading to fragmentation -> eventual CUDA OOM under normal load. Likely a regression in the allocator's free-path when attention paging is enabled.

eng-carol: reproducer locally: run long chat loop with long context (50k tokens) and alternating model sizes — kv_cache grows and never evicts. Adding logs: `KVCache::free_list` remains non-empty but not coalescing freed pages.

infra-miguel: mitigation plan (short): 1) roll global config to lower KV cache high-water threshold; 2) trigger rolling restart of affected node pool with pinned runtime image to clear fragmentation; 3) enable temporary per-pod aggressive eviction.

eng-carol: executing step 1 — patching configmap `runtime-config` to set `KV_CACHE_EVICT_TARGET=0.25` and `PAGED_ALLOC_FRAG_LIMIT=0.4`. Applying now: ```kubectl -n prod patch configmap runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"KV_CACHE_EVICT_TARGET":"0.25","PAGED_ALLOC_FRAG_LIMIT":"0.4"}}'```

deploy-bot: Rollout started for configmap/runtime-config in namespace prod. Notifying replicas to pick up new config (via configmap reload sidecar).

eng-carol: forcing rolling restart on runtime-kv-pool-3 to pick up config and free GPU allocations: ```kubectl -n prod rollout restart statefulset/runtime-kv-pool-3 --timeout=10m```

infra-miguel: initiating node drain + restart on nodes with highest frag ratios (usw2-17, usw2-19). We'll cordon, drain, then restart GPU driver to clear leaked GPU allocations if any.

support-lina: updating status page: short degradation for serving-runtime in us-west-2, engineering investigating. (will post customer-facing note after we confirm mitigation) :eyes:

eng-carol: added debug env `RUNTIME_ALLOC_DEBUG=1` to affected pods (via transient annotation) to collect allocator histograms, and turned on periodic KVGC every 5m as a temporary measure.

sre-alex: immediate results: after rollout and restarts, error rate for affected pool dropped from 4.8% -> 1.1% in 12 minutes. Memory metrics: `kv_cache_total_bytes` trend flattened on restarted pods but still rising on a subset that hasn't rotated yet.

infra-miguel: one node (usw2-17) flapped during drain — kubelet reported image pull timeout; we recovered and re-scheduled pods elsewhere. No further flaps after we bumped kubelet `image-pull-timeout` on nodegroup.

eng-carol: captured allocator debug dump (snippet): ```free_buckets: [64,128,256] counts: [12,3,0] allocated_pages: 123456 frag_ratio: 0.47 last_compaction: 2026-03-14T22:41:03Z``` Looks like compaction path isn't running for paged-attention case (condition check gated on `active_sessions == 0` which isn't happening). We need a long-term fix.

sre-lead: next steps (mid/long-term): - Roll a hotfix to force periodic compaction even with active sessions (runtime PR queued) - Add alert for `kv_cache_total_bytes` slope > X over 30m - Add e2e test for paged-attention leak with sustained long-context sessions - Postmortem and customer communication once stable

eng-carol: opened PR #4872 with a small change to compaction trigger + unit tests; running CI now. If safe, we'll promote to canary in us-west-2 tomorrow morning.

support-lina: customer comms: drafted message for affected customers: "We experienced elevated errors due to allocator fragmentation leading to GPU OOMs. We deployed mitigations (config change + restarts) and are monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause and permanent fix." Want approvals before sending.

sre-alex: approved. Send on the status page and to customer contacts.

deploy-bot: Noted: configmap/runtime-config patch applied. rollout restart completed for statefulset/runtime-kv-pool-3. 8/8 pods restarted successfully.

eng-carol: follow-up action items I added to tracker: link to logs, allocator dumps, PR reference, proposed regression test, and a runbook entry for live mitigation steps (lower eviction target, force compaction, restart strategy).

sre-alex: handing over to oncall rotation for monitoring and post-incident follow-ups. If error rate rises above 2% in next 30m, page SRE lead and runtime eng oncall.

support-lina: done — customers notified, status page updated.

incident-bot: Incident marked as mitigated at 1768003741 (temporary mitigations applied). Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC.

sre-alex: thanks all. Good coordination. We'll treat this as Sev2 with a follow-up Sev2 postmortem and fix timeline.

eng-carol: adding one final note — consider adding a canary steady-state test that exercises large prefix reuse (KV heavy) nightly to catch slow creeps earlier.

sre-lead: agreed, adding to engineering radar.
